title: Northwind Customer Onboarding
summary: Northwind Onboarding is the tool the Onboarding Officer uses to set up a new customer. The officer first searches by postcode and surname so that no duplicate record is created, then enters the customer's details, uploads a photo of their ID and reviews a summary before submitting the record for approval. Submission locks the record and places it in the Approval Queue. A Team Lead approves it from the queue, which produces a Confirmation screen with a customer reference number that the officer gives to the customer. The system then sends a welcome email to the address entered.
actors: Document checker (role not named by the expert, see Q001)

actions.description: Enters the postcode and surname and presses Search; the matching existing customers are listed below
Presses Open on a result row to view an existing customer
Presses Create new customer when the customer is not already on the system
Picks the account type (Personal or Business) from the Account type dropdown
Ticks 'Customer has given marketing consent' when the customer has said yes
Presses Save and continue after filling in the mandatory details
Chooses a file for the ID document, picks the Document type from the dropdown and presses Upload; the document appears in the Uploaded documents table with status Pending check
Reads the summary and presses Submit for approval; the record is locked and appears in the Approval Queue
A team lead presses Approve on an 'Awaiting approval' row
Presses Start another customer to begin the next onboarding

journey.description: The Onboarding Officer enters the postcode and surname on Customer Search and presses Search to see whether the customer already exists.
When the customer is not in the results, the Onboarding Officer presses Create new customer.
The Onboarding Officer fills in the mandatory details (First name, Last name, Date of birth, Account type, Postcode) plus any optional details on Customer Details.
The Onboarding Officer ticks marketing consent only when the customer said yes, then presses Save and continue.
On Documents, the Onboarding Officer chooses the ID file, picks the Document type and presses Upload; the document appears in the table with status Pending check.
Someone the expert could not name checks the document and its status changes to Verified.
The Onboarding Officer presses Continue to review.
The Onboarding Officer reads the Review & Submit summary and presses Submit for approval; the record is then locked for editing.
The submitted customer appears in the Approval Queue with status Awaiting approval and an assignee; a Team Lead presses Approve.
After approval the Confirmation screen shows the customer reference number, which the Onboarding Officer gives to the customer.
The system sends a welcome email to the email address entered on Customer Details.

requirements.statement: The system lists the existing customers that match the entered postcode and surname when the Onboarding Officer presses Search.
requirements.rationale: Customer Search is the first step of onboarding and exists to stop duplicate customer records.
requirements.source_quote: You put in the postcode and the surname and hit Search, and it lists anyone we already have, so you don't create a duplicate.

requirements.statement: The system shows Customer ID, Name, Date of birth, Postcode, Account type and Status for each customer in the search results.
requirements.rationale: The six columns are visible on the results table in frame 0; the expert did not name them.
requirements.source_quote: it lists anyone we already have

requirements.statement: The system shows the number of matches in the heading above the search results.
requirements.rationale: Frame 0 shows the heading 'Results (3 matches)'.
requirements.source_quote: it lists anyone we already have

requirements.statement: The system shows an Open button on every row of the search results.
requirements.rationale: Open appears on every row in frame 0, including the Closed customer; where it leads was not shown (see Q008).
requirements.source_quote: it lists anyone we already have

requirements.statement: The system opens Customer Details when the Onboarding Officer presses Create new customer.
requirements.rationale: The Create new customer button sits under the results table in frame 0 and the expert described the move to Customer Details.
requirements.source_quote: If they're new, you go to Customer Details.

requirements.statement: The system requires First name, Last name, Date of birth, Account type and Postcode before it saves a new customer.
requirements.rationale: The five fields are marked * on screen and the expert named them as mandatory.
requirements.source_quote: First name, last name, date of birth, account type and postcode are mandatory; the rest we fill in when we have it.

requirements.statement: The system saves a new customer when Email address, Phone number, Address line 1, Address line 2 and Town / City are blank.
requirements.rationale: None of these fields is marked * on screen; the expert said the address lines and town are optional and the rest is filled in when available.
requirements.source_quote: The address lines and the town are optional.

requirements.statement: The system saves Customer Details only when the Postcode is in a valid UK postcode format.
requirements.rationale: Hint under the field reads 'UK postcode format, e.g. SW1A 1AA'. The exact pattern and the error message were not shown (see Q006).
requirements.source_quote: The postcode has to be a valid UK format, otherwise the system won't let you save.

requirements.statement: The Account type dropdown offers exactly two options: Personal and Business.
requirements.rationale: Both values also appear in the Customer Search results.
requirements.source_quote: Account type is a dropdown, personal or business

requirements.statement: The Onboarding Officer ticks 'Customer has given marketing consent' only when the customer has said yes.
requirements.rationale: Business rule stated by the expert. The value is carried to Review & Submit as Marketing consent Yes or No.
requirements.source_quote: the marketing consent box only gets ticked if the customer actually said yes

requirements.statement: The system opens Documents when the Onboarding Officer presses Save and continue with valid Customer Details.
requirements.rationale: Save and continue is the primary button on Customer Details; the expert went straight on with 'Next is Documents'.
requirements.source_quote: Then you press Save and continue.

requirements.statement: The system adds the chosen file to the Uploaded documents table when the Onboarding Officer presses Upload with a file chosen and a Document type selected.
requirements.rationale: ID document and Document type are both marked * on screen. The full list of document types was not shown (see Q010).
requirements.source_quote: We upload a photo of their ID, usually a passport or a driving licence, and pick the document type from the dropdown.

requirements.statement: The system accepts ID document files in PDF, JPG or PNG format.
requirements.rationale: Taken from the hint text under the ID document control: 'PDF, JPG or PNG, up to 10 MB'. Not mentioned by the expert.
requirements.source_quote: We upload a photo of their ID

requirements.statement: The system accepts ID document files up to 10 MB in size.
requirements.rationale: Taken from the hint text under the ID document control: 'PDF, JPG or PNG, up to 10 MB'. Not mentioned by the expert.
requirements.source_quote: We upload a photo of their ID

requirements.statement: The system shows File, Document type, Uploaded, Uploaded by and Status for each row of the Uploaded documents table.
requirements.rationale: The five columns are visible in frame 2; the expert named only the status column.
requirements.source_quote: The status column shows pending until the document has been checked.

requirements.statement: The system sets the status of a newly uploaded document to 'Pending check'.
requirements.rationale: Frame 2 shows the badge 'Pending check' (amber) on the passport row.
requirements.source_quote: The status column shows pending until the document has been checked.

requirements.statement: The system changes the status of a document to 'Verified' when the document has been checked.
requirements.rationale: Frame 2 shows the badge 'Verified' (green) on the proof of address row. Who checks, and where, is unknown (see Q001).
requirements.source_quote: Someone checks them, I'm honestly not sure who, it just changes to verified at some point.

requirements.statement: Review & Submit shows the entered Name, Date of birth, Email address, Phone number, Address, Account type, Marketing consent and ID document as read-only text.
requirements.rationale: The summary rows are visible in frame 3. The proof of address document is not listed there (see Q010).
requirements.source_quote: Review and Submit is a summary of everything so far. You read it through, and if it all looks right you press Submit for approval.

requirements.statement: The system makes the customer record read-only after the Onboarding Officer presses Submit for approval.
requirements.rationale: Also stated on screen: 'After submission the record is locked for editing.'
requirements.source_quote: Once you submit, the record locks and you can't edit it any more.

requirements.statement: The system adds the customer to the Approval Queue with status 'Awaiting approval' when the Onboarding Officer presses Submit for approval.
requirements.rationale: Priya Shah, submitted in the recording, appears in the queue in frame 4 with the badge 'Awaiting approval'.
requirements.source_quote: Every submitted customer sits here with a status

requirements.statement: A Team Lead sends a submitted customer record back to the Onboarding Officer for editing.
requirements.rationale: The expert was unsure and no send-back control was seen. Needs confirming before it is built (see Q005).
requirements.source_quote: You'd have to ask a team lead to send it back, I think.

requirements.statement: The Approval Queue shows Reference, Customer, Submitted, Submitted by, Status, Assigned to and Action for every submitted customer.
requirements.rationale: The seven columns are visible in frame 4; the expert named status and assignee.
requirements.source_quote: Every submitted customer sits here with a status, and it shows who it's assigned to

requirements.statement: The Approval Queue orders customers by Submitted date and time with the oldest at the top.
requirements.rationale: The subtitle in frame 4 reads 'Customers submitted for approval, oldest first', but the Approved row (08/09/2026 11:14) is last, which contradicts it (see Q016).
requirements.source_quote: Every submitted customer sits here with a status

requirements.statement: The system shows the Approve action only to users in the Team Lead role.
requirements.rationale: Banner on screen: 'Team leads only. The Approve action is shown to users in the Team Lead role. Other users can view the queue but cannot approve.' The frame contradicts this (see Q003).
requirements.source_quote: Only team leads can approve. The Approve button doesn't show for the rest of us, and it says team leads only at the top.

requirements.statement: The system lets a user outside the Team Lead role view the Approval Queue.
requirements.rationale: The banner says other users can view the queue, and the expert, an Onboarding Officer, is viewing it in the recording.
requirements.source_quote: The Approve button doesn't show for the rest of us, and it says team leads only at the top.

requirements.statement: The system sets the status of a customer to 'Approved' when a Team Lead presses Approve on that customer's row.
requirements.rationale: Frame 4 shows the badge 'Approved' (green) with a dash in the Action column on the approved row.
requirements.source_quote: Only team leads can approve.

requirements.statement: The system shows the approver assigned to each submitted customer in the Assigned to column.
requirements.rationale: Assigned to shows 'Lena Fischer' and 'Unassigned' in frame 4. The rule for choosing the assignee is unknown (see Q002).
requirements.source_quote: it shows who it's assigned to, though I've never worked out how it picks the person

requirements.statement: The system shows the Confirmation screen with the Customer reference number after a customer is approved.
requirements.rationale: The reference is shown large in monospace in frame 5 and matches the Approval Queue row for the same customer.
requirements.source_quote: When it's approved, you get the Confirmation screen with a reference number. We give that reference to the customer.

requirements.statement: The Confirmation screen shows Approved by with the approver's name and role, and Approved on with the date and time of approval.
requirements.rationale: Frame 5 shows 'Approved by: Lena Fischer (Team Lead)' and 'Approved on: 10/09/2026 10:31'. Not mentioned by the expert.
requirements.source_quote: When it's approved, you get the Confirmation screen

requirements.statement: The system gives each submitted customer a unique reference in the form NW-YYYY-NNNNN.
requirements.rationale: Inferred from the references seen: NW-2026-04409, NW-2026-04412, NW-2026-04415, NW-2026-04417. The reference already exists in the Approval Queue, so it is created at submission (see Q017).
requirements.source_quote: you get the Confirmation screen with a reference number

requirements.statement: The system sends a welcome email to the Email address entered on Customer Details when the customer is approved.
requirements.rationale: Frame 5 shows 'Welcome email: Sent to priya.shah@example.com'. Bounce handling and a blank address are open (see Q004, Q013).
requirements.source_quote: A welcome email goes out automatically to the address we entered.

requirements.statement: The Confirmation screen shows the welcome email status with the address the email was sent to.
requirements.rationale: Frame 5 shows only 'Sent to <address>'; no bounce or delivery status is shown.
requirements.source_quote: A welcome email goes out automatically to the address we entered.

questions.question: Who checks uploaded documents and changes their status from 'Pending check' to 'Verified', and on which screen do they do it?

questions.context_quote: Someone checks them, I'm honestly not sure who, it just changes to verified at some point.

questions.question: How is the 'Assigned to' approver chosen for a submitted customer, and why are some rows 'Unassigned'?
questions.why_it_matters: The assignment rule must be specified before the queue can be built; Priya Shah's row shows Unassigned while other rows show Lena Fischer.
questions.context_quote: it shows who it's assigned to, though I've never worked out how it picks the person

questions.question: Frame 4 shows Approve buttons while signed in as Jo Patel, Onboarding Officer. Is that a test setting, does Jo also hold the Team Lead role, or should Approve be hidden for everyone outside the Team Lead role?
questions.why_it_matters: The expert's words and the banner say only Team Leads see Approve, but the screen shows it to an Onboarding Officer; the permission rule must be confirmed.
questions.context_quote: The Approve button doesn't show for the rest of us, and it says team leads only at the top.

questions.question: What should happen when the welcome email bounces: who is told, does the Confirmation screen show the failure, and can the email be resent?
questions.why_it_matters: Today a bounce goes unnoticed, so a customer may never get their welcome email.
questions.context_quote: If the email bounces it just sort of sits there, nobody gets told.

questions.question: Can a submitted (locked) record be sent back for editing, who can do it, and what happens to its Approval Queue row and reference number?
questions.why_it_matters: The expert was unsure whether Team Leads can unlock a record; without this, a mistake found after submission has no fix path.
questions.context_quote: You'd have to ask a team lead to send it back, I think.

questions.question: What exactly counts as a valid UK postcode (pattern, spacing, upper or lower case), and what error message is shown when it fails?
questions.why_it_matters: The developer needs the validation rule and the error behaviour to implement the save block.
questions.context_quote: The postcode has to be a valid UK format, otherwise the system won't let you save.

questions.question: Must a search be run before Create new customer can be pressed, and what does the screen show when the search finds no matches?
questions.why_it_matters: The duplicate check only works if the search cannot be skipped; the no-match state was not shown.
questions.context_quote: it lists anyone we already have, so you don't create a duplicate.

questions.question: What does the Open button on a search result do, and what should happen for a customer whose Status is Closed (for example Anil Shah)?
questions.why_it_matters: Open is shown on every row including a Closed customer, but the expert did not say where it leads or whether a closed customer can be onboarded again.

questions.question: Does the search match on both postcode and surname, and how exact is the match? One result shows postcode SW1A 1AB although SW1A 1AA was entered.
questions.why_it_matters: The matching rule decides which existing customers are found and whether duplicates slip through.
questions.context_quote: You put in the postcode and the surname and hit Search

questions.question: Which document types are in the Document type dropdown, and is a proof of address document required as well as an ID document?
questions.why_it_matters: The expert mentioned only passport or driving licence, but the table shows a 'Proof of address' upload, and Review & Submit lists only the ID document.
questions.context_quote: We upload a photo of their ID, usually a passport or a driving licence, and pick the document type from the dropdown.

questions.question: Can a record be submitted for approval, and then approved, while its ID document is still 'Pending check'?
questions.why_it_matters: Review & Submit shows the ID document as 'Pending check' with Submit for approval available, so the dependency between verification and approval is unclear.
questions.context_quote: You read it through, and if it all looks right you press Submit for approval.

questions.question: Are Date of birth (DD/MM/YYYY, age limits), Email address and Phone number validated, and what are the rules?
questions.why_it_matters: Only the postcode rule was stated; the hint DD/MM/YYYY suggests format checking but nothing was said about it.
questions.context_quote: First name, last name, date of birth, account type and postcode are mandatory; the rest we fill in when we have it.

questions.question: If Email address is left blank on Customer Details (it is optional), what happens to the welcome email on approval?
questions.why_it_matters: The welcome email goes to the entered address, but the address is not mandatory.
questions.context_quote: A welcome email goes out automatically to the address we entered.

questions.question: How does the Onboarding Officer reach the Confirmation screen after a Team Lead approves, and are they told of the approval or a rejection?
questions.why_it_matters: Approval is done by a different person, possibly later, so the officer's path to the Confirmation screen and the reference number is not shown.
questions.context_quote: When it's approved, you get the Confirmation screen with a reference number.

questions.question: Can a Team Lead reject a submitted customer, and which statuses exist besides 'Awaiting approval' and 'Approved'?
questions.why_it_matters: Only an Approve action was shown; a rejection path and its statuses are needed to complete the approval workflow.

questions.why_it_matters: The sort order and whether approved rows remain decide how the queue is built and how long it grows.
